slides.headline: This week in India's growth story.
5 stories.
listItems: He grew up the son of a cobbler in rural Maharashtra. Today, his company has over 4,500 employees.
Sixteen Fortune 500 companies are run by Indian-origin CEOs. Together, they generate more revenue than most countries' entire economies.
She became the first Indian-origin, first woman of color to lead a 131-office global ad network.
After three years of debate, one language was chosen to speak for an entire country.
India just hit a climate target five years ahead of schedule. And it wasn't close.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: India's electronics exports jumped 57% in a single month.
Every satellite India launches needs a processor that can survive space. Until last year, none of them were built entirely in India.
Reshma Kewalramani was born in Bombay and moved to the US at age 11. In 2020, she became the first woman to lead a large public biotech company.
A ditch-digger's daily wage was ₹300. An Asian Games bronze medal doesn't ask what you used to do for money.
The UN General Assembly had never had a woman president. Then it did.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: Optical cameras can't see through clouds. Radar can't see color or texture. One Bengaluru startup just put both on a single satellite - a world first.
India's exports just crossed $860 billion in a single year.
In 1989, a young physicist solved a puzzle nobody else could explain. In 2026, that work made him the first Indian-origin scientist to win the Wolf Prize in Physics.
He lost his right arm at five. At the Commonwealth Games, he ran the 100m faster than anyone in the field ever had.
No musician had ever received India's highest civilian honor. Then one did.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: India's chip industry just had its busiest funding year yet.
A tractor took his leg at 17. Nine years later, he'd broken his own javelin world record for the second time.
Immigrants founded or co-founded 59% of America's billion-dollar startups. No country contributed more of them than India.
He spent his career as a government bureaucrat. He also became one of India's greatest living poets.
Six hyperspectral satellites are already in orbit, built by one Bengaluru company. It just raised $100 million to build a lot more.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: Most factory robots can only do one job, on one object, forever. One Bengaluru startup built a robot that can pick up almost anything, untrained.
India just had its best August for car sales ever recorded.
Robbers threw her off a moving train for her gold chain. Two years later, she stood on top of the world.
India's highest cinema honor went to a director who never chased a single award.
The Arthur M. Bueche Award has existed for over four decades. No Indian American had ever won it - until now.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: Every chip in an Indian car, phone or inverter used to come from Taiwan, China or Vietnam. In July, a Gujarat plant shipped its first batch out - to a customer in Japan.
If the global Indian diaspora were counted as its own economy, it would outrank about 170 of the world's roughly 195 countries. Not from remittances. From what it earns.
He started at P&G in 1989 as an assistant brand manager. In January 2026, he became its CEO.
A state education board told a blind teenager he couldn't study science. So he sued them - and won.
A Bombay lawyer never performed music in public. He's the reason Indian classical music has a written notation at all.

slides.headline: 5 stories.
listItems: The Indian diaspora doesn't just earn abroad. A new report says it's closing a billion-dollar philanthropy gap to become one of America's most generous immigrant communities.
She started on a factory floor. She now runs a $27.9 billion company - and is about to spin off another.
Doctors wanted to amputate his leg as a schoolboy. His family said no - and he became a Paralympic silver medalist.
He built India's first digital computer. Decades later, he built the machine that counts India's votes.
Every EV motor and wind turbine needs a rare earth magnet. Last year, India imported 93% of them from one country. Last month, 20 companies bid to change that.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Every week adds another piece.
slides.body: None of these stories are the whole picture on their own - the picture is what they add up to, one week at a time, for the next 20 years.
